feed.title: NPR Topics: News
feed.subtitle: Breaking news, top national and world stories, politics, business and culture from NPR. Catch up on demand with NPR News Now, Up First and Consider This.

entry.title: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
entry.summary: The current outbreak, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now counted 10,000 patients and has spread with great speed. How can it be stopped?

entry.title: A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month
entry.summary: A federal judge has barred the government from clearing more trees or making other alterations to D.C.'s East Potomac Park without proper notice. Trump says his administration will appeal.

entry.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
entry.summary: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.

entry.title: Discursive Verses: Jay-Z, the Super Bowl and playing with house money
entry.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: Is the rap mogul's self-selection a crowning achievement or a final affront?

entry.title: A 'Green Army' is out to thwart El Niño flooding
entry.summary: In Nairobi, a city prone to floods, workers in the "Green Army" are making preparations to prevent disaster when El Niño arrives.

entry.title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
entry.summary: Democrats are still holding a slight edge with Election Day a week away, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. And, Israelis are casting their votes in an election that could change leadership.

entry.title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
entry.summary: The German-owned chain's low prices are winning over shoppers — and pushing competitors to respond.

entry.title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
entry.summary: Mississippi has the largest proportional Black population in the country. It's one reason the U.S. Senate race has seen millions in last-minute spending and high-profile campaign visits.

entry.title: Polymarket has investigated 'dozens' of election-related cases
entry.summary: The prediction market has hired a former FBI official to make sure political insiders don't use the platform for profit from confidential election information.

entry.title: Democrats still poised to make gains, but poll shows warning signs for just how many
entry.summary: Democrats hold significant advantages going into Election Day, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. But lagging enthusiasm among key groups is just one indicator that gains may not come easy.
